sources.title: Genomic history of early dogs in Europe
sources.authors_or_org: Bergström, A., Furtwängler, A., Johnston, S. et al.
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed Nature ancient-genome study; 216 canid remains, oldest genome-wide dog data around 14,200 years.

sources.title: Dogs were widely distributed across western Eurasia during the Palaeolithic
sources.authors_or_org: Marsh, W.A., Scarsbrook, L., Yüncü, E. et al.
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed Nature ancient-genome study; Pınarbaşı and Gough’s Cave Palaeolithic dogs and cross-cultural distribution.

sources.title: Grey wolf genomic history reveals a dual ancestry of dogs
sources.authors_or_org: Bergström, A., Stanton, D.W.G., Taron, U.H. et al.
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed Nature study of 72 ancient wolf genomes across 100,000 years.

sources.title: Origins and genetic legacy of prehistoric dogs
sources.authors_or_org: Bergström, A., Frantz, L., Schmidt, R. et al.
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed Science ancient-dog genome study; 27 ancient dog genomes.

sources.title: A new look at an old dog: Bonn-Oberkassel reconsidered
sources.authors_or_org: Janssens, L., Giemsch, L., Schmitz, R. et al.
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed Journal of Archaeological Science reanalysis of Bonn-Oberkassel dog remains.

sources.title: The genomic signature of dog domestication reveals adaptation to a starch-rich diet
sources.authors_or_org: Axelsson, E., Ratnakumar, A., Arendt, M.L. et al.
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed Nature comparative genomics study identifying selection signals related to starch digestion.

sources.title: Amy2B copy number variation reveals starch diet adaptations in ancient European dogs
sources.authors_or_org: Ollivier, M., Tresset, A., Bastian, F. et al.
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed Royal Society Open Science ancient-dog study of AMY2B copy number.

sources.title: Oxytocin-gaze positive loop and the coevolution of human-dog bonds
sources.authors_or_org: Nagasawa, M., Mitsui, S., En, S. et al.
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed Science experiment on modern dog–human gaze and oxytocin; not direct evidence for Palaeolithic domestication.

sources.title: Commensalism or Cross-Species Adoption? A Critical Review of Theories of Wolf Domestication
sources.reliability_note: Critical scholarly review of competing domestication scenarios; useful for framing uncertainty, not for proving one mechanism.
